extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to Wellcome Open Research (and similar journals) who need to respond to peer review feedback
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for authors on how to read, organise, implement, and reply to peer reviewer comments (within an open peer review model). Focuses on documenting revisions, drafting a response letter, and strategies for when to accept or decline changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the open peer review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research uses an open peer review model, where reports are public and the identities of authors and reviewers are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace transparency: this approach encourages constructive feedback, speeds up publishing, enhances research impact, increases accountability, acknowledges reviewers by publicising their names and reviews, and can help authors trust reviewer expertise. Understanding this model is essential for effectively addressing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read all reviewer comments carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you receive the reviewer comments, take the time to read them thoroughly and understand them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers often provide both general feedback and specific comments or suggestions. Don’t rush—thorough reading helps you identify the substantive issues and appropriate responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: List all requested changes in a new document
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing reviewer feedback, list all the changes the reviewers have requested by moving them into a new document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use line numbers or bullet points to separate the feedback and include a separate section for comments from each reviewer. This creates a clear, organised record to track revisions and draft replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorise each comment (four-category scheme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider separating each comment into one of four main categories to prioritise and plan responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four categories are: (1) Valid and essential suggestions — clear issues or improvements that significantly enhance quality; (2) Comments that require clarification — misunderstandings or requests for more information; (3) Comments that can be politely declined — suggestions that don’t align with your goals or fall outside scope; (4) Comments about minor revisions — small changes that don’t affect conclusions (e.g., missing references, data presentation, typos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight changes and use track changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark where you will make edits in the manuscript and visualise them with track changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning where to make changes and turning on track changes helps you locate edits later when writing your response letter and makes it easier for reviewers/editors to see what you changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy reviewer feedback into manuscript comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert reviewer comments into the manuscript as comments to map suggestions to specific locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copying feedback into comments within the manuscript helps understand where edits should be placed and how different suggestions relate to each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify points reviewers misunderstood
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers point out aspects you believe are already explained, use this as an opportunity to clarify rather than assume misunderstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a few additional sentences or references to explain that part of your research further—if one person is confused, others may be as well. Ensure clarifications do not appear as if you overlooked feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide and explain where changes cannot be made
rubrics_metrics.description: Think carefully about where changes cannot or should not be made—e.g., if they require a lot more research or change the focus of your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is a discussion: it is acceptable to politely disagree with reviewers. If you decline a suggestion, explain your rationale clearly in the response letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a clear, structured response letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a response document that thanks reviewers, organises replies with clear headings, and quotes reviewers directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a brief introduction thanking the reviewers. Organise the letter with clear headings for each reviewer’s comments, quote reviewers briefly, and explain your responses. Use examples and set revisions apart with italics or text boxes for emphasis. Keep tone respectful and professional. A good response can be fairly long if it is well structured and easy to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a respectful, professional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout your responses and revisions, keep your language courteous and professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thank reviewers for their time and feedback and emphasise your commitment to improving your work. Respectful tone supports constructive dialogue and collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for further rounds of review
rubrics_metrics.description: After resubmitting, be ready for additional peer review rounds and further revision requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach subsequent rounds with the same professionalism and commitment. Peer review is a collaborative effort aimed at advancing knowledge; continued engagement with reviewers improves quality and impact.
